title: Community ideas. Youth leadership.
description: A locally adaptable gathering model that connects teenagers’ service ideas with the strengths of their communities.
---

::: {.status}

Program model in development

:::


TSP’s signature model is a community gathering where teenagers identify local strengths and opportunities, develop youth-led service proposals, present their ideas, and receive support from neighbors. Young people then work toward implementation and share what they learned.

Support can be practical: a meeting space, transport, materials, mentorship, a useful introduction, or volunteer time. Financial contributions and small grants can help when available, but they are **not requirements for participation or hosting**.

## From an idea to shared learning

::: {.steps}

1. **Prepare together.** Listen to young people, map community strengths, identify access needs, and agree on realistic expectations.
2. **Develop service ideas.** Teens choose an opportunity that matters locally, describe a manageable first step, and identify what support would help.
3. **Gather as a community.** Create an accessible setting for proposals, conversation, questions, and offers of assistance.
4. **Connect projects with support.** Match ideas with people, resources, spaces, and optional funding. Avoid making success depend on a popularity contest.
5. **Put ideas into practice.** Youth teams and adult supporters agree on responsibilities, check in, and adapt to what is feasible.
6. **Reflect and improve.** Share experiences, what changed, what did not work, and what another community should know.

:::


These are proposed components, not a tested sequence or mandatory event format. A small gathering in a familiar space can be a useful starting point.

## Where the model draws inspiration

The concept is a youth-centered adaptation of the community-supported project model associated with [Detroit SOUP](https://detroitsoup.com/), informed by asset-based community development and youth participatory leadership. Educational resources, project development, and participant support associated with the [Diamond Challenge](https://diamondchallenge.org/), and collaborative team service experiences associated with [Public Allies](https://publicallies.org/), are additional conceptual reference points.

These references describe inspiration, **not partnerships, endorsements, or a claim to reproduce those organizations’ programs**.

## Resources will develop through use

Original TSP materials will be reviewed before guides, worksheets, or implementation examples are published. We will distinguish proposed guidance from practices supported by documented experience.

[Browse the resource archive](resources/index.qmd), [see the development plan](resources/development.qmd) and [how communities can contribute learning](feedback.qmd).
